capabilities.title: Cinematic Rendering Pipeline
capabilities.subtitle: Physical-based HDR pipeline surpassing soup3D — mip-chain bloom, atmospheric scattering, morphological AA and more.

bloom.title: UnrealBloom
bloom.desc: 5-level mip Gaussian bloom with soft-knee threshold and lens dirt.

sky.title: SkyAtmosphere
sky.desc: GPU ray-marched Rayleigh + Mie + Ozone multi-scatter sky.

smaa.title: SMAA
smaa.desc: Subpixel Morphological Antialiasing with procedural LUTs.

gtao.title: GTAO
gtao.desc: Ground Truth ambient occlusion via hemisphere horizon integration.

sss.title: SSSS
sss.desc: Screen-space subsurface scattering for skin translucency.

hairMarschner.title: Marschner Hair
hairMarschner.desc: Physically-based hair BCSDF (Marschner 2003): R / TT / TRT three-lobe scattering with dielectric Fresnel and Beer-Lambert pigment absorption. UE5/HDRP-grade hair rendering.

taa.title: TAA
taa.desc: Temporal antialiasing with Halton jitter and history clipping.

motionBlurEnhanced.title: Motion Blur (Enhanced)
motionBlurEnhanced.desc: Depth-aware motion blur with 3×3 neighbor velocity min-clamp and Halton(2,3) jittered sampling. Eliminates ghosting at object edges and streaking at velocity discontinuities. Adaptive sample count scales with pixel velocity.

sssr.title: Stochastic SSR
sssr.desc: GGX importance-sampled screen-space reflections with temporal accumulation for physically correct rough reflections.

volfog.title: Volumetric Fog
volfog.desc: Ray-marched volumetric fog with god rays and scattering.

volcloud.title: Volumetric Clouds
volcloud.desc: GPU ray-marched volumetric clouds with 3D Perlin+Worley noise, Beer-Powder transmittance, dual-lobed HG phase (silver-lining), and multi-scattering.

cloudShadow.title: Cloud Shadows
cloudShadow.desc: Volumetric cloud shadows ray-marched along the sun direction through the same 3D noise field as the sky clouds, applying Beer-Lambert transmittance to darken the scene. Silhouettes stay in sync with drifting clouds and the sun angle.

caustics.title: Underwater Caustics
caustics.desc: Screen-space caustics with 3 modes: procedural 3-sine, Gerstner normal-focusing, and hybrid. RGB dispersion + Beer-Lambert + water-line fade. CPU + GPU 1:1.

waterSurface.title: Water Surface
waterSurface.desc: Screen-space planar water with 4-directional Gerstner waves, Schlick Fresnel reflection/refraction blend, Beer-Lambert depth absorption, and Blinn-Phong sun specular.

godRays.title: God Rays
godRays.desc: Screen-space volumetric light shafts (crepuscular rays) with radial sampling, luminance-threshold extraction, exponential decay, and depth-aware occlusion — ~10x cheaper than VolumetricFog.

lensFlare.title: Lens Flare
lensFlare.desc: Screen-space lens flare with ghost chain, RGB chromatic aberration, gaussian halo ring, and starburst rays — depth-occluded, off-screen faded, ~5x cheaper than GodRays.

gpuParticles.title: GPU Particles
gpuParticles.desc: GPU particle system with RGBA32F texture ping-pong simulation, MRT single-pass integrate, POINTS + gl_VertexID fetch rendering — 65536+ particles, zero CPU readback.

localExposure.title: Local Exposure
localExposure.desc: Log-space local-global luminance difference driven exposure compensation — brightens shadows, darkens highlights, preserves detail. Complements AutoExposure for HDR scenes.

lensDistortion.title: Lens Distortion
lensDistortion.desc: Brown-Conrady radial lens distortion with optional RGB chromatic aberration — barrel (wide-angle) / pincushion (telephoto), principal-point offset, scale compensation. OpenCV/o3de-grade camera optics.

screenSpaceRefraction.title: Screen-Space Refraction
screenSpaceRefraction.desc: Snell's law refraction for arbitrary transparent surfaces (glass, ice, water puddles, holograms) with RGB chromatic dispersion and Beer-Lambert absorption. Generalizes planar Refractor to any shape.

heightFog.title: Height Fog
heightFog.desc: UE5-style exponential height fog with closed-form Beer-Lambert density and sun inscattering.

ssgi.title: SSGI Screen-Space Global Illumination (o3de Atom / UE5 Lumen)
ssgi.desc: Screen-Space Global Illumination CPU reference implementation adapted from Crytek SSDO (Ritschel 2009), o3de Atom ScreenSpaceGlobalIllumination, UE5 Lumen Screen Space GI, and EA SEED Stable SSAO. Cosine-weighted hemisphere sampling (8 rays) with Interleaved Gradient Noise (IGN) jittering, TBN basis construction, view-space thickness hit test, adaptive step size (near-small far-large), edge fade + distance attenuation + cosine weight. Production-grade features beyond basic SSGI_FRAG: temporalAccumulate() with velocity-based reprojection + 3x3 neighborhood clamping (ghost suppression), denoiseSpatial() edge-preserving bilateral filter (normal+depth weights), varianceClip() SVGF-style statistical outlier clipping. Pure functions, no WebGL dependency, runnable in Node/headless. 91 unit tests. Complements SSR (specular) + GTAO (occlusion) + DDGI (world-space low-frequency).
ssgi.advantage: soup3D has no GI at all (no SSGI, no DDGI, no light probes); VREEN has full GI stack: SSGI + DDGIVolume + GlobalIllumination + PathTracer

ddgi.title: DDGI
ddgi.desc: Dynamic diffuse global illumination with 3D irradiance probe grid, SH2 directional storage, and real-time relighting.

pcss.title: PCSS
pcss.desc: Percentage-closer soft shadows with blocker search and penumbra estimation.

csm.title: Cascaded Shadow Maps
csm.desc: PSSM cascaded shadow maps (2-8 cascades). Logarithmic+uniform split, tight texel utilization, cascade blending for seamless transitions. Essential for large outdoor scenes.

lut.title: LUT Grading
lut.desc: 3D/2D strip LUT color grading with .cube file support.

decal.title: Decals
decal.desc: Projected decal system with lifetime, fading, and normal alignment.

skin.title: Skin SSS
skin.desc: Pre-integrated skin BSSRDF with d'Eon 2007 diffuse/transmittance LUTs.

sharpen.title: CAS Sharpen
sharpen.desc: AMD FidelityFX contrast-adaptive sharpening. Restores TAA-softened detail.

fsr.title: FSR Upscale
fsr.desc: FidelityFX FSR1 edge-adaptive spatial upscaling. Render at 50-70% resolution.

tsr.title: Temporal Super Res
tsr.desc: UE5-class temporal upscaler. Halton jitter + reprojection + neighborhood clamp + confidence blend reconstructs sub-pixel detail across frames, approaching native resolution quality at 50-70% render cost.

specularAA.title: Specular AA
specularAA.desc: Toksvig/LEAN filtering. Eliminates specular shimmer on bumpy normals at distance.

svgf.title: SVGF Denoiser
svgf.desc: Spatiotemporal Variance-Guided Filtering. 3-stage denoiser (temporal accumulation + variance estimation + a-trous wavelet) for 1-spp SSR/SSGI/path-tracing.

screenSpaceDecal.title: Screen-Space Decals
screenSpaceDecal.desc: GPU deferred decals projected onto GBuffer geometry. Volume + angle culling, 4 blend modes (Alpha/Multiply/Additive/Normal), edge fade, ping-pong multi-decal chaining.

autoExposure.title: Auto Exposure
autoExposure.desc: Eye adaptation: downsampled logarithmic luminance average + exponential adaptation curve. Simulates human pupil response when moving between dark/bright areas.

dof.title: Depth of Field (CoC + Bokeh)
dof.desc: Production-grade DoF adapted from Potmesil & Chakravarty 1981, GPU Gems 1 Ch.23, three.js BokehShader, and o3de Atom DepthOfFieldBokehBlurPass. Computes Circle of Confusion (CoC) from view-space depth via inverse projection: CoC = clamp(|dist - focusDistance| / focusRange, 0, 1). 16-direction bokeh sampling with three shape kernels: circle (default), hexagon (6-edge diamond, r=0.866), octagon (max(|cos|,|sin|), r=0.924). Configurable: focusDistance, focusRange, bokehShape (0/1/2), bokehSize (px), maxRadius (px, clamps GPU cost). Skybox passthrough (depth >= 0.99999). Sub-pixel radius skip (< 0.5px = sharp). 1:1 CPU/GPU reference (dofReconstructViewPos / dofBokehWeight / computeCoC / dofBokehRadius / dofSampleColor / dofPixel / computeDOF) for headless testing and offline rendering. 54 unit tests. RGBA16F output for HDR bokeh highlights.

contactShadows.title: Contact Shadows
contactShadows.desc: Screen-space directional shadow rays from depth buffer. Fills small-scale contact occlusion where CSM/PCSS can't reach — under props, characters, vehicles.

tonemapping.title: Tone Mapping
tonemapping.desc: HDR to LDR tone mapping: ACES Filmic, Reinhard, AGX, Uncharted2, Linear. Essential for HDR pipelines with physically-based lighting.

terrain.title: Terrain System
terrain.desc: Heightmap terrain with chunked LOD, hydraulic+thermal erosion simulation, splatmap texturing, real-time terrain editor, FBM noise generation.

vegetation.title: Vegetation System
vegetation.desc: Instanced foliage rendering with wind animation, density-based placement via surface sampling, multiple vegetation types, LOD-based culling.

voxel.title: Voxel World
voxel.desc: Chunked voxel world with palette-based block types, raycaster for block selection/placement, greedy meshing, Minecraft-style building mechanics.

physics.title: Physics Engine
physics.desc: Rigid body + cloth + soft body + fluid + rope + ragdoll + vehicle + flight + buoyancy + Voronoi fracture + destruction. Constraint solver, collision detection, physics materials.

ai.title: AI System
ai.desc: NavMesh + pathfinding + GOAP planner + utility AI + perception (sight/hearing) + crowd steering + blackboard + ML interface. Complete game AI toolkit.

ik.title: Inverse Kinematics
ik.desc: CCD + FABRIK solvers, IK chain/bone hierarchy, constraint-aware joint limits. Procedural foot placement, hand reaching, look-at targeting.

paniniProjection.title: Panini Projection
paniniProjection.desc: Cylindrical wide-FOV projection (Sharpless/o3de Atom). Keeps vertical lines straight while allowing wider horizontal FOV without edge stretching. depth parameter controls intensity; optional vertical mode for panoramic/360° output. Architectural viz + cinematic wide-angle.

colorGrading.title: Color Grading
colorGrading.desc: Single-pass ASC-CDL color grading (8 parameters: temperature/tint/saturation/contrast/gain/lift/gamma/hueShift). DaVinci-style lift/gamma/gain + white balance + hue rotation. Runtime-tunable fields for animation system integration.

outline.title: Outline Pass
outline.desc: Selection highlight outline (three.js OutlinePass adapted to CPU). Mask → separable Gaussian blur → edge subtraction → alpha blend. Configurable edge color / strength / blur radius / glow. Editor/inspector object selection highlighting.

reflectionProbe.title: Reflection Probe
reflectionProbe.desc: Local IBL cube capture (6-face 90° render → cube texture). AABB influence volume (position + boxSize + priority). Optional PMREM prefilter (Karis 2013 split-sum GGX importance sampling → RGBA16F mip chain) for physically-correct roughness-dependent specular IBL. Per-probe re-capture on geometry change.

lookModification.title: Look Modification (ASC-CDL)
lookModification.desc: ASC-CDL 1.2 industry-standard color decision list (Slope/Offset/Power + Saturation). Interoperable with DaVinci Resolve / Nuke / Baselight via .cdl XML. Pure CPU ascCDL() reference + GPU pass. Auto-skips GPU work on identity transform. Film-grade look exchange, normally only in Unreal/o3de.

lutBlender.title: LUT Blender
lutBlender.desc: Multi-LUT hierarchical blender (o3de BlendColorGradingLutsPass adapted). Blends up to 4 color grading LUTs by priority + intensity + overrideStrength, generating a single blended LUT for LUTPass. Enables smooth day/night color transitions, mood/area switches, narrative effects with 1 LUT sample/pixel. Pure CPU, dirty-tracking, headless-testable.

luminanceHistogram.title: Luminance Histogram
luminanceHistogram.desc: 128-bin EV100 luminance histogram + auto-exposure eye adaptation (o3de LuminanceHistogramGeneratorPass adapted). Percentile-clipped weighted average ignores extreme pixels (bright sky / deep shadow) for robust target EV. Asymmetric adaptation (fast brightening / slow darkening) matches human pupil response. Rec709 luma, EV100=log2(L*8), range [-8,16]. Pure CPU, headless-testable, can drive GPU EyeAdaptationPass.
luminanceHistogram.advantage: soup3D only has basic log-average auto-exposure

whiteBalance.title: White Balance (Bradford CAT)
whiteBalance.desc: Physically-based white balance via Bradford chromatic adaptation transform (o3de WhiteBalancePass adapted). temperature/tint → CIE xy → LMS cone response → per-channel scale. Preserves relative color ratios unlike naive RGB shifts. Matches camera/cinema white balance (ISO/CIE 11664-3, ACES IDT). CPU reference whiteBalance() + GPU pass. Identity skip on (0,0). Apply in linear space before tonemapping.
whiteBalance.advantage: soup3D has no white balance feature

outputTransform.title: ACES Output Transform (10 Tonemappers + PQ HDR)
outputTransform.desc: Industry-standard ACES output transform adapted from o3de Atom OutputTransform.azsl + Tonemap.azsli + Aces.azsli. 10 tonemappers: Reinhard, ReinhardExtended, AcesFitted (Stephen Hill fit), AcesFilmic (Narkowicz), Filmic (Hable Uncharted 2), AgX family (AgX/AgxGolden/AgxPunchy/AgxWarm — Blender/Filament), PbrNeutral (Khronos). ACEScg → sRGB color space conversion via precomposed matrix (XYZ_TO_SRGB * D60_TO_D65 * AP1_TO_XYZ). 2 transfer functions: Gamma 2.2 (SDR) and SMPTE ST 2084 PQ (HDR10). EV exposure compensation + cinema black/white point mapping. 1:1 CPU/GPU reference. Final pipeline stage.
outputTransform.advantage: soup3D has only 1 basic tonemapper, no color space conversion, no HDR output

sao.title: Scalable Ambient Obscurance (SAO)
sao.desc: Performance-oriented screen-space ambient occlusion adapted from three.js SAOPass.js + SAOShader.js (McGuire, Mara, Luebke 2012, HPG). Spiral sampling pattern (default 7 samples × 4 rings = 28 taps), each sample contributes occlusion in O(1). Occlusion formula: max(0, (dot(N, delta) - minRes) / scaledDist - bias) / (1 + scaledDist²). Faster than GTAO (28 samples vs 128), ideal for mobile/VR/large-scale scenes. Configurable kernelRadius, intensity, bias, scale, numSamples, numRings, randomSeed. Per-frame random rotation reduces banding. Skybox detection + boundary clamping. 1:1 CPU/GPU reference implementation.

fxaa.title: FXAA 3.11 Enhanced (3 Quality Presets)
fxaa.desc: Industry-standard FXAA 3.11 (Timothy Lottes, NVIDIA 2009) with 3 quality presets: Console (4-step edge walk, fastest), PC High (8-step, balanced default), PC Extreme (10-step, best quality). Full algorithm: Rec601 luma → local contrast detection → edge direction (H/V gradient) → decreasing-length edge endpoint search → blend factor (edge + subpixel). Configurable subpixel (0.75), edgeThreshold (1/6), edgeThresholdMin (1/16). Single-pass, no extra buffers needed. Supersedes basic FXAAPass (2-step search). 1:1 CPU/GPU reference. VREEN now offers 3 complementary AA techniques: FXAA + SMAA + TAA.
fxaa.advantage: soup3D has no anti-aliasing at all

fastDepthAwareBlur.title: Fast Depth-Aware Blur (o3de Atom H+V)
fastDepthAwareBlur.desc: Depth-aware separable blur adapted from o3de Atom FastDepthAwareBlurPasses (Horizontal + Vertical). Walks the blur direction one texel at a time, comparing consecutive depth slopes to detect edges and reduce mix weight at depth discontinuities — preventing foreground/background color bleeding (halo artifact). Building-block pass for AO/SSGI/Bloom/DoF that need edge-preserving blur. Standard Gaussian crosses depth edges producing halos; depth-aware variant confines blur to same depth layer. H+V dual-pass (ping-pong FBOs), O(2*blurRadius) samples/pixel. Configurable blurRadius (1..32), constFalloff (2/3), depthFalloffThreshold (0), depthFalloffStrength (50). 1:1 CPU/GPU reference (calculateDepthFalloff / blurDirection / fastDepthAwareBlurPixel). Algorithm core identical to o3de Atom; VREEN trades compute/LDS optimizations for WebGL2 portability.

bloomEnhanced.title: Bloom Enhanced (Depth-Aware Edge-Preserving)
bloomEnhanced.desc: Depth-aware edge-preserving Bloom that reuses the FastDepthAwareBlur algorithm (H+V separable, depth-slope edge stopping) to confine bloom to the same depth layer, preventing foreground/background color bleeding (halo) that classic Gaussian or box-blur bloom produces across silhouettes. Pipeline: Bright pass (soft knee, Rec.709 luminance threshold) → FastDepthAwareBlur H → FastDepthAwareBlur V → Composite (additive + lens dirt + RGB tint). 4 GPU dispatches per apply, HDR RGBA16F. Configurable strength, threshold, smoothWidth, blurRadius (1..32), depthFalloffStrength, per-channel tint, optional lens dirt texture + dirtStrength. 1:1 CPU/GPU reference (luminance / brightPassPixel / bloomCompositePixel). Complementary to UnrealBloomPass (multi-mip large glow) — stack both for glow + clean edges. Ideal for neon/cyberpunk high-contrast scenes.
bloomEnhanced.advantage: soup3D has only single box-blur bloom

lightingChannel.title: Lighting Channels (32-bit Mask, o3de/Unreal)
lightingChannel.desc: Lighting channels adapted from o3de Atom LightingChannelConfiguration. Each light and each renderable carries a 32-bit channel mask; at render time a light only contributes to a fragment if (lightMask & objectMask) != 0. Default = ALL channels (backward compatible — every light lights every object). Use cases: player flashlight that only lights the player (not the environment), muzzle flash that lights enemies + nearby props (not the whole map), UI/emissive panels that don't pollute character lighting, indoor lights that don't leak outdoors, trigger-zone lights. o3de ships 5 channels; VREEN extends to 32 (Unreal-aligned). LightingChannelConfiguration class with fluent API (setChannel/enableChannel/disableChannel/setSingleChannel/reset/clear/affects/toJSON/fromJSON/clone) + pure helpers (channelMask/channelsMask/getChannel/setChannel/affects/countChannels/listChannels) + GLSL chunk (lightingChannelAffects). 68 unit tests.

hzbOcclusion.title: Hierarchical Z-Buffer Occlusion Culling (o3de/UE5)
hzbOcclusion.desc: HZB occlusion culling adapted from o3de Atom MaskedOcclusionCulling / OcclusionCullingPlane and UE5 HZB. Builds a mip pyramid from the depth buffer where each level stores the MAX depth of its 2×2 children (conservative — never falsely culls visible objects). For each object's AABB, projects 8 corners to screen space, selects mip level based on screen rect size (log2), samples HZB depth at rect center, and culls if object's nearest depth > HZB depth. Greene 1993 algorithm. Configurable: conservativeBias (reduces false positives), mipBias, minScreenSize (skips tiny objects). Pure CPU Float32Array (no WebGL dependency, testable in Node/headless). Complements frustum culling — culls in-frustum objects behind walls/mountains. Use cases: indoor scenes (walls cull behind), open world (terrain culls behind), GPU-driven rendering (batch cull thousands of objects). GLSL chunk (hzbReduceMax2x2 / hzbIsOccluded) for future GPU integration. 35 unit tests.

areaLightLTC.title: Area Light LTC (Heitz 2016)
areaLightLTC.desc: Linearly Transformed Cosines area light evaluation adapted from Heitz, Dupuy, Hill, Neubelt 2016 'Real-Time Polygonal-Light Shading with Linearly Transformed Cosines', three.js LTC.js, and o3de Atom LtcCommon.cpp. Evaluates rectangular area light irradiance using LTC matrix transform: constructs orthonormal basis around surface normal, transforms light vertices into canonical cosine space via inverse LTC matrix, projects onto unit sphere, computes 4-edge vector form factors with rational polynomial theta/sin(theta) approximation, applies horizon clipping. Supports specular + diffuse lobes. LUT sampling (ltcUv) for 64x64 precomputed LTC matrices parameterized by roughness x dot(N,V). Handles degenerate case when V parallel to N. Configurable: focusDistance, focusRange, bokehShape. Pure CPU functions (ltcEvaluate, evaluateRectAreaLight, computeAreaLighting, approximateLTCMatrix, makeRectVertices) for headless testing. 49 unit tests.
areaLightLTC.advantage: soup3D only has point/directional lights, no area lights

meshletRenderer.title: Meshlet Renderer (UE5 Nanite / o3de)
meshletRenderer.desc: Meshlet rendering pipeline adapted from three.js meshopt_clusterizer, o3de Atom MeshletsModule, and UE5 Nanite. Splits large meshes into small clusters (meshlets, max 256 vertices / 512 triangles each) for fine-grained visibility culling. Each meshlet has independent bounding sphere + normal cone (apex + axis + cutoff cos). Full culling pipeline: frustum cull (bounding sphere vs 6 planes) + backface cull (normal cone: dot(viewDir, axis) >= cutoff) + HZB occlusion cull (project bounding sphere, select mip by projected radius, sample HZB depth). Visible meshlets packed into indirect draw commands with cumulative vertexOffset/firstIndex. Merged vertex/index buffers for GPU upload. Pure CPU, no WebGL/WASM dependency, testable in Node/headless. 42 unit tests.
meshletRenderer.advantage: soup3D has no meshlet or GPU-driven rendering

visibilityBuffer.title: Visibility Buffer (UE5 Nanite / o3de Atom)
visibilityBuffer.desc: Visibility buffer deferred rendering adapted from o3de Atom VisibilityBuffer.azsli + DeferredMaterial and UE5 Nanite. Stores per-pixel geometry IDs (meshInfoIndex + triangleId + barycentrics + isFrontFace) instead of full GBuffer attributes, halving bandwidth and decoupling material types from geometry pass. o3de Atom-compatible bit packing: 2 RGBA32F texels per pixel (flagsAndMeshInfoIndex with bit 31=invalid, bit 30=frontFace, bits 29..0=meshInfoIndex; triangleId; barycentrics.xy with z=1-x-y reconstructed; barycentricsDx/Dy.xy with z=-x-y reconstructed). Empty pixel marker: -0.0f (0x80000000) vs valid +0.0f (meshInfoIndex=0). CPU software rasterizer (edge-function barycentric + depth test + visbuf write). Full pipeline: pack -> rasterize -> build -> getMeshInfoIndex (fast path) -> unpack -> decompressPixel -> fetchTriangleVertices -> interpolateAttributes -> shade. GLSL chunks (VISIBILITY_BUFFER_PACK_VERT/FRAG with GL_EXT_fragment_shader_barycentric, VISIBILITY_BUFFER_UNPACK_UTILITY for deferred shading). Natural companion to MeshletRenderer for UE5 Nanite GPU-driven loop. Pure CPU, no WebGL dependency, testable in Node/headless. 75 unit tests.
visibilityBuffer.advantage: soup3D has no visibility buffer or deferred material system

esm.title: Exponential Shadow Maps (o3de Atom)
esm.desc: Exponential Shadow Maps (ESM) CPU reference implementation adapted from o3de Atom EsmShadowmapsPass + DepthExponentiationPass, Salvi 2008 'Fast Shadow Maps on a 1K Budget', and Annen et al. 2008 'Exponential Shadow Maps'. Converts shadow map depth to exp(c·d) domain so that linear/Gaussian filtering becomes mathematically valid (no PCF aliasing), enabling hardware bilinear sampling of pre-filtered shadow maps. Visibility formula matches o3de ESM.azsli SampleESM 1:1: visibility = clamp(exp(-c·d_receiver) · ESM[u,v], 0, 1). Pipeline: expDepthMap (depth exponentiation) -> filterESM (separable Gaussian or box H+V blur) -> sampleESM (1-tap bilinear on pre-filtered texture) or sampleESMFiltered (inline N×N box). Soft shadows at 1-9 taps vs PCSS 16-41 taps. Configurable exponent c (16-bit textures: ≤11, 32-bit: ≤80), bias, wrap mode, kernel (gaussian/box), radius, sigma, separable flag. Includes sampleESMPCF for cross-validation. GLSL chunk ESM_SAMPLE_GLSL provides matching GPU functions (sampleESM, sampleESMBox, expDepth). Complements ShadowMapManager (basic/PCF/PCSS) giving VREEN 4 shadow solutions covering full quality-performance spectrum. Pure CPU Float32Array, no WebGL dependency. 51 unit tests.
esm.advantage: soup3D has basic hard shadows only, no ESM / soft shadows / PCSS

pom.title: Parallax Occlusion Mapping (o3de Atom)
pom.desc: Parallax Occlusion Mapping (POM) CPU reference + GLSL chunks adapted from o3de Atom ParallaxMapping.azsli, RTR4 §6.7.1, Tartachuk 2004 'Parallax Occlusion Mapping', and Riccardi 2018 'Contact Refinement Parallax Mapping'. Ray-marches through a height map in tangent space to give flat textured surfaces (brick walls, cobblestones, embossed tiles) convincing 3D geometric depth without adding vertices. 5 algorithms: basic (1-tap offset), steep (multi-step ray march), pom (steep + linear interpolation, AAA standard), relief (steep + binary search refinement), contact (Riccardi 2018 high-precision fewer-sample). Optional self-shadowing (march from intersection toward light to detect occlusion, producing soft crevice shadows). Optional Pixel Depth Offset (PDO) — converts tangent-space offset back to world space and recomputes gl_FragDepth for correct depth testing and shadow receiving. 4 quality presets matching o3de: Low=16 / Medium=32 / High=64 / Ultra=128 steps. Depth range guard (stopDepth - startDepth < 0.0001 returns 0) matches o3de edge-case handling. Wrap modes: clamp/repeat. Pure CPU Float32Array reference + 3 GLSL chunks (PARALLAX_BASIC_CHUNK, PARALLAX_POM_CHUNK, PARALLAX_RELIEF_CHUNK) directly embeddable in WebGL2 fragment shaders. 61 unit tests.
pom.advantage: soup3D has normal mapping only (flat, no depth); no POM / relief / contact refinement / self-shadow / PDO

vsm.title: Virtual Shadow Maps (UE5 / o3de Atom)
vsm.desc: Virtual Shadow Maps (VSM) CPU reference implementation adapted from UE5 Virtual Shadow Maps (Engstrom & Persson, SIGGRAPH 2021) and o3de Atom VirtualShadowMapPass. Treats the shadow frustum as a virtual texture divided into fixed-size pages (128x128 texels), allocated on-demand into a physical atlas (8192x8192, 4096 pages). Distant regions use lower mip levels based on screen-space texel density ratio (texelRatio), achieving per-pixel shadow resolution adaptation — near surfaces get high-resolution pages, far surfaces get coarse mip pages. No fixed-resolution limit, no CSM seam artifacts. PageTable class with LRU eviction, gc() for frame-based page reclaim. Mip selection: floor(log2(texelRatio / texelDensity)), clamped to [0, maxMipLevels-1]. Virtual resolution pyramid: 2048 -> 1024 -> 512 -> 256 -> 128 texels (5 mip levels). PCF 4-tap soft edges. GLSL chunk VSM_SAMPLE_GLSL with vsmSample(), vsmSamplePCF4(), vsmSelectMipLevel(), vsmPackPageUV() for WebGL2. Complements ShadowMapManager (basic/PCF/PCSS), CSM, and ESM — VREEN now has 5 shadow solutions covering full resolution/performance spectrum. Pure CPU Float32Array, no WebGL dependency. 74 unit tests.
vsm.advantage: soup3D has fixed-resolution shadow maps only (2048/4096); no adaptive per-pixel shadow resolution, no virtual page atlas

meshshader.title: Mesh Shader Pipeline (o3de Atom / NVIDIA Turing)
meshshader.desc: Mesh Shader Pipeline (Task Shader + Mesh Shader) CPU reference implementation adapted from o3de Atom MeshShaderPass / MeshShaderDispatchItem, NVIDIA Turing Mesh Shaders (SIGGRAPH 2019), and Vulkan VK_EXT_mesh_shader. Replaces traditional IA -> VS -> HS -> DS -> GS -> RS -> PS pipeline with Task Shader -> Mesh Shader -> RS -> PS. Task Shader runs in workgroups of 32 meshlets, performing per-meshlet culling on GPU: LOD distance + frustum (sphere vs 6 planes) + normal-cone backface + HZB occlusion, compacting visible meshlets into TaskDispatchItem[]. Mesh Shader transforms vertices to clip space and does per-triangle backface culling. WebGL2 does not natively support Mesh Shaders; this module provides CPU reference (pure functions, no WebGL dependency, runnable in Node/headless) + GLSL chunks (TASK_SHADER_GLSL, MESH_SHADER_GLSL) for future WebGL2 emulation or WebGPU integration. Complements MeshletRenderer (CPU meshlet construction) -> meshletBoundsToCullData() bridges the two. 14 exported functions + types, 74 unit tests, mat4Multiply column-major. Combined with MeshletRenderer + VisibilityBuffer + HierarchicalZBuffer, VREEN has a complete GPU-driven rendering stack matching UE5 Nanite and o3de Atom MeshletsModule.
meshshader.advantage: soup3D uses only traditional IA + VS pipeline for all geometry, submitting each mesh as a whole without per-meshlet culling, no Task/Mesh Shader, no GPU-driven dispatch

meshDistanceField.title: Mesh Distance Field (UE5 / Hart 1996)
meshDistanceField.desc: Mesh Distance Field (MDF) + Distance Field Soft Shadows (DFSS) + Distance Field Ambient Occlusion (DFAO) CPU reference implementation, adapted from UE5 Mesh Distance Fields + Distance Field Shadowing + Distance Field Ambient Occlusion, Hart 1996 Sphere Tracing, Crassin et al. 2011 Voxel Cone Tracing, and Ericson 2005 Real-Time Collision Detection 5.1.5 (point-triangle distance). Encodes mesh surfaces as a 3D uniform grid signed distance field (positive outside, zero on surface, negative inside). Sphere tracing advances along a ray by the current SDF value each step, guaranteeing no surface penetration: no aliasing, no acne, no bias tuning, natural soft shadows from cone tracing. The same SDF is reusable for shadows (DFSS cone tracing with penumbra = d / (t * lightSize)), ambient occlusion (DFAO Fibonacci hemisphere sampling), collision, GI, and particle collision. World-space solution complementing the light-space shadow family (basic / PCF / PCSS / ESM / VSM / CSM): light-space maps are bounded by texture resolution and projection geometry; SDF is bounded only by voxel resolution, independent of view/light. Golden-ratio direction (1, phi^-1, phi^-2) for inside-test parity counting avoids axis-aligned edge/vertex degeneracies. Minimum bias = 2x voxelSize (resolution-derived, not scene-tuned). Trilinear sampling matches GLSL texture(sampler3D, LINEAR). Ray-AABB entry computation allows shadows from points outside the mesh AABB. 68 unit tests, pure functions, no WebGL dependency, runnable in Node/headless. GLSL chunks (SDF_SAMPLE_GLSL, DFSS_SHADOW_GLSL, DFAO_GLSL) for future GPU integration. VREEN now has 6 shadow solutions (basic / PCF / PCSS / ESM / VSM / DFSS) covering the full performance-quality spectrum, with DFSS as the only world-space option.
meshDistanceField.advantage: soup3D has only basic hard shadows with bias-tuning artifacts; no signed distance field, no world-space shadow solution, no distance field ambient occlusion, single-purpose shadow maps only

virtualTexturing.title: Sparse Virtual Texture (o3de / UE5)
virtualTexturing.desc: Sparse Virtual Texture (SVT) system adapted from o3de Atom Virtual Texture (Gems/Atom/Asset/ImageStreaming), UE5 Virtual Texturing (TexturePageTable + FeedbackBuffer), Mellor 2004 Virtual Texture Mapping, and Niesner 2009 Practical Virtual Texture Rendering. Pages ultra-large virtual textures (e.g., 16384x16384) into fixed-size 128x128 tiles, loading only the pages actually sampled by the GPU into a shared physical texture atlas (default 8192x8192 = 4096 slots). Uses the same PageTable (mip + pageX + pageY -> physicalIndex) + PhysicalAtlas pattern as VirtualShadowMap (shadow-space paging). GPU writes feedback (sampled pages) via MRT; CPU processes feedback, deduplicates, sorts by mip (lower = higher resolution = higher priority) and sampleCount, then loads pages capped at maxPagesPerFrame (default 8) to prevent frame-rate spikes. LRU eviction with priority weighting (score = lastUsed - priority * 1000) prevents thrashing. preloadLowMips pre-loads 1x1 and 2x2 fallback pages. Complements TextureStreaming (mip-level streaming for many medium textures): SVT handles single huge textures (terrain mega-texture, satellite imagery, 8K+ character textures) beyond GPU memory limits. virtualUVToPhysicalUV remaps shader UVs through the page table. 50+ unit tests, pure CPU reference, no WebGL dependency. GLSL chunks (VIRTUAL_TEXTURE_GLSL, VT_FEEDBACK_GLSL, VT_PAGE_TABLE_GLSL) for GPU integration.
virtualTexturing.advantage: soup3D has no texture streaming system at all, no virtual texturing, no page-based loading, cannot handle textures larger than GPU memory limit; VREEN has both TextureStreaming (mip streaming) and VirtualTexturing (page-based SVT) covering all texture streaming scenarios

voxelConeTracing.title: Voxel Cone Tracing GI (Crassin 2011)
voxelConeTracing.desc: Voxel Cone Tracing Global Illumination (VXGI) CPU reference implementation, adapted from Crassin et al. 2011 Interactive Indirect Illumination Using Voxel Cone Tracing and El Garawany 2013 SIGGRAPH course. Builds a 3D voxel representation of the scene (occupancy + color + normal), constructs a mip chain for multi-resolution anisotropic sampling, then traces cones through the voxel volume to compute both diffuse GI (N wide cones on Fibonacci hemisphere, default 6 at 30 degrees) and specular GI (1 narrow cone along reflect direction, half-angle = roughness * pi/4, Schlick Fresnel). The cone radius grows linearly with distance (t * tan(halfAngle)), and the mip level is selected as log2(coneRadius / voxelSize), so distant samples use coarser mips (anisotropic filtering, analogous to texture mipmapping). Pre-multiplied alpha blending with early termination (occlusion < 0.99) accumulates color and occlusion front-to-back. The same voxelization provides diffuse GI, specular GI, and ambient occlusion from a single pass. Voxel-space GI complementing the existing GI family: SSGI (screen-space, visible only), DDGI (probe-based, needs placement), VXGI (voxel-space, off-screen, no probes), LPV (grid-space, fastest multi-bounce), PathTracer (offline, highest quality). Covers off-screen surfaces (unlike SSGI) without probe placement (unlike DDGI). 40+ unit tests, pure CPU reference, no WebGL dependency. GLSL chunks (VOXEL_CONE_TRACING_GLSL, VOXELIZATION_GLSL, VOXEL_MIP_CHAIN_GLSL) for GPU integration. VREEN now has 5 GI methods (SSGI + DDGI + VXGI + LPV + PathTracer) covering all quality-performance tradeoffs.
voxelConeTracing.advantage: soup3D has no global illumination system at all; VREEN has 5 GI methods (SSGI + DDGI + VXGI + LPV + PathTracer) covering screen-space, probe-based, voxel-space, grid-space, and offline path-traced GI, with VXGI providing off-screen indirect lighting without probe placement

lightPropagationVolume.title: Light Propagation Volumes GI (Kaplanyan 2009)
lightPropagationVolume.desc: Light Propagation Volumes (LPV) CPU reference implementation, adapted from Kaplanyan 2009 Light Propagation Volumes in CryEngine 3 and Kaplanyan & Dachsbacher 2010 Propagation of Radiance. Injects direct lighting (point, directional, emissive surfaces) into a 3D Spherical Harmonics (SH2) grid (9 basis x 3 RGB = 27 floats per cell), iteratively propagates radiance through 6 axis-aligned face directions to neighboring cells with double-buffering (each iteration = one bounce, default 4), and samples via trilinear interpolation of 8 neighboring cells' SH coefficients + evaluateSH at the surface normal. SH2 captures low-frequency diffuse indirect lighting (sufficient for diffuse, use ReflectionProbe/SSR for specular). Optional geometry occlusion volume (Uint8Array) blocks light propagation through solid geometry, preventing light leaking in indoor scenes (build via buildGeometryVolume from triangle meshes). Grid-space GI complementing the existing GI family: SSGI (screen-space, visible only), DDGI (probe-based, needs placement), VXGI (voxel-space, needs voxelization), LPV (grid-space, fastest multi-bounce, no probes, no voxelization), PathTracer (offline, highest quality). LPV covers off-screen surfaces (unlike SSGI) without probe placement (unlike DDGI) or expensive voxelization (unlike VXGI) - light propagation is a simple SH evaluation per cell face, extremely fast O(N^3 x iterations x 6), ideal for real-time multi-bounce GI on low-end hardware. 61 unit tests, pure CPU reference, no WebGL dependency. GLSL chunks (LPV_GLSL, LPV_INJECTION_GLSL, LPV_PROPAGATION_GLSL) for GPU integration via 3D textures + compute shaders. VREEN now has 5 GI methods (SSGI + DDGI + VXGI + LPV + PathTracer) - the most comprehensive GI stack in any web-based engine.
lightPropagationVolume.advantage: soup3D has no global illumination system at all; VREEN has 5 GI methods (SSGI + DDGI + VXGI + LPV + PathTracer) covering screen-space, probe-based, voxel-space, grid-space, and offline path-traced GI, with LPV providing the fastest real-time multi-bounce GI without probes or voxelization - ideal for low-end hardware

layeredPBRMaterial.title: Layered PBR Material (o3de Material Layering)
layeredPBRMaterial.desc: Layered PBR Material CPU reference implementation, adapted from o3de's Material Layering system. Allows stacking up to 8 PBR material layers on a single mesh, each with independent albedo / metallic / roughness / normal / emissive / AO / height, plus a grayscale mask (Float32Array) controlling the layer's blend weight across the surface. 4 blend modes: normal (lerp), add (accumulation, wetness/glow), multiply (darkening, shadowing), overlay (Photoshop-style contrast, weathering). Bilinear mask sampling with WRAP UV addressing (tiling), per-layer UV scale/offset. Optional vertex color alpha modulates the mask (grass on top faces, snow on upward surfaces). Normal blending with separate normalBlend factor [0,1] + re-normalization. Emissive is always additive across layers (glowing runes over painted surface + glowing cracks). Static mask factory methods: createFullMask (uniform), createRadialMask (impact decals, splatter), createNoiseMask (scratches, rust, dirt, deterministic with seed). Typical use cases: car paint (metal + paint + scratches + rust + dirt), terrain (rock + grass + dirt + snow), character (skin + grime + blood + wear), weapon (metal + coating + wear + rust), wall (plaster + cracks + mold + graffiti). 56 unit tests, pure CPU reference, no WebGL dependency. GLSL chunks (LAYERED_PBR_GLSL, LAYERED_PBR_VERTEX_GLSL, LAYERED_PBR_FRAGMENT_GLSL) for GPU integration via MaterialLayer[MAX_LAYERS] uniform array + mask samplers. soup3D has only single material per mesh; VREEN supports professional material layering essential for game and film production.
layeredPBRMaterial.advantage: soup3D only supports a single material per mesh with no layering; VREEN supports up to 8 PBR layers with per-layer masks, 4 blend modes, vertex color modulation, and mask factory methods - essential for professional game and film production (car paint, terrain, character, weapon, wall layering)

vrs.title: Variable Rate Shading (o3de Atom / UE5)
vrs.desc: Variable Rate Shading (VRS) tile classification system adapted from o3de Atom AZ::RHI::ShadingRate + RasterPass::FragmentShadingRate, UE5 VariableRateShading plugin, and VK_KHR_fragment_shading_rate / D3D12 VRS. Divides the screen into tiles (8x8 / 16x16 / 32x32 pixels) and assigns each tile a shading rate (1x1 full / 1x2 / 2x1 / 2x2 quarter / 2x4 / 4x2 eighth / 4x4 sixteenth), so the GPU shades fewer pixels in low-sensitivity regions. 4 composable classification strategies: MotionVRS (fast-moving pixels -> lower rate, motion blur hides detail), DepthVRS (flat surfaces -> lower rate, depth gradient analysis), FoveatedVRS (peripheral vision -> lower rate, gaze-point based, essential for VR), LuminanceVRS (low-contrast areas -> lower rate, luminance variance analysis). VRSTileClassifier combines all strategies taking the most conservative (highest) rate per tile. MultiResolutionCompositor provides a WebGL2 software fallback (low-rate tiles rendered at reduced resolution then composited). 4 presets: performance / balanced / quality / vr. GLSL chunks (VRS_GLSL, VRS_FEEDBACK_GLSL) for future WebGPU / hardware VRS integration. Complements TAA/TSR (VRS provides performance, TAA/TSR reconstructs detail) and HZB (HZB culls invisible objects, VRS reduces visible-area shading). 50 unit tests, pure CPU, no WebGL dependency.
vrs.advantage: soup3D has no Variable Rate Shading, no foveated rendering, no tile-based shading rate classification; VREEN provides 4 classification strategies + software fallback + hardware VRS readiness — critical for VR and high-resolution performance

motionMatching.title: Motion Matching (UE5 Pose Search / o3de EMotionFX)
motionMatching.desc: Motion Matching — a next-generation data-driven animation selection system, adapted from Kovar 2002 Motion Graphs (SIGGRAPH), Clavet 2016 Motion Matching (GDC, Ubisoft For Honor), UE5 Pose Search plugin, and o3de EMotionFX MotionMatching. Replaces hand-built animation state graphs with a search problem: (1) Offline build — sample motion-capture clips at fixed intervals, extract per-frame feature vectors (trajectory = past N + current + future M points with posX/posZ/facing/speed; pose = key joint positions + velocities for feet/hands/root); (2) Runtime search — from player input build a desired trajectory, linear-scan the database to find the minimum-cost frame (cost = weighted sum of trajectory position + facing + speed differences + pose difference, with future points weighted higher via futureMultiplier). If best cost < maxSwitchCost, switch to that frame with blendTime crossfade. 4 presets: precise (per-frame search, always switch, fighting/action), balanced (0.1s search, cost<1.0, RPG/adventure), performance (0.2s search, cost<0.5, open world/MMO), cinematic (never search, cutscenes). Cost weights follow Clavet 2016 GDC recommendations (pos=1.0, facing=1.0, speed=0.5, pose=0.8, futureMult=1.5). Composes with AnimationMixer (decision layer vs execution layer) and FootPlacementIK (post-processes pose to prevent foot sliding). 45 unit tests, pure CPU, no WebGL dependency.
motionMatching.advantage: soup3D only has a traditional animation state machine requiring manual state graph construction; VREEN provides data-driven Motion Matching that searches a database to find the best transition frame automatically — natural transitions, responsive to player input, no manual state graph needed (UE5 Pose Search / o3de EMotionFX class technology)

orca.title: ORCA Collision Avoidance (RVO2 / Van den Berg 2011 SIGGRAPH)
orca.desc: ORCA — Optimal Reciprocal Collision Avoidance, a velocity-space crowd avoidance solver adapted from Van den Berg et al. 2011 (SIGGRAPH) and the RVO2 reference library, with integration reference from UE5 MassAI DetourCrowd and o3de RecastNavigation DetourCrowd. Replaces Reynolds separation force (used by CrowdSystem) which suffers from force-sum jitter, no future prediction, and pile-ups at narrow passages. Algorithm (per agent per frame): (1) collect neighbors via distance-sorted query capped at maxNeighbors; (2) for each neighbor compute an ORCA half-plane line {direction, point} — if not colliding, build a truncated velocity obstacle (cut-off circle when relative velocity projects outside the cone, tangent legs when inside, left/right chosen by 2D determinant sign); if colliding, project onto a timeStep cut-off circle to force immediate separation; responsibility is split 50/50 so line.point = agent.velocity + 0.5*u; (3) three-stage linear program (LP1 finds the closest-to-preferred velocity on a line intersected with the maxSpeed circle clipped to [tLeft, tRight]; LP2 walks constraints from optVelocity and calls LP1 on first violation; LP3 is the 3D LP fallback that projects onto subsequent lines, guaranteeing a feasible velocity even when over-constrained). 4 presets: denseCrowd (small radius, short horizon, low speed — subway/mall/combat), openBattlefield (large radius, long horizon, high speed — RTS/vehicles), cityTraffic (medium, stability-focused — traffic/pedestrians), highPrecision (long horizon, many neighbors — cutscenes/key NPC). 2D XZ-plane solve matches CrowdSystem (Y ignored). 39 unit tests. Composes with CrowdSystem as a drop-in avoidance layer (CrowdSystem keeps Reynolds as default, ORCA is opt-in for dense crowds).
orca.advantage: soup3D only has Reynolds steering separation force (reactive, jittery in dense crowds, no future collision prediction, pile-ups at narrow passages); VREEN provides RVO2 ORCA velocity-space solving — proactive future-collision avoidance within timeHorizon, symmetric 50/50 responsibility, jitter-free dense crowds, queue-through narrow passages, and immediate separation when already colliding (UE5 DetourCrowd / o3de RecastNavigation class technology)

uiSystem.title: In-Game UI System (o3de LyShine / UE5 UMG / Unity UI Toolkit)
uiSystem.desc: A complete in-game UI stack adapted from o3de LyShine, UE5 UMG (Unreal Motion Graphics), and Unity UI Toolkit. UICanvas with 3 render modes (ScreenSpaceOverlay / ScreenSpaceCamera / WorldSpace) and 3 scale modes (ConstantPixelSize / ScaleWithScreenSize with reference resolution + matchWidthOrHeight log-space interpolation / ConstantPhysicalSize DPI-based). RectTransform with 16 anchor presets (point + stretch), pivot, offsets, sizeDelta. Two-phase auto-layout: HorizontalLayoutGroup / VerticalLayoutGroup / GridLayoutGroup (spacing/padding/alignment/controlChildSize/ flexibleSpaces/childForceExpand) + ContentSizeFitter (min/preferred/unconstrained) + LayoutElementPrefs. Widgets: UIText (alignment/wrap/overflow/lineSpacing + content-driven sizing), UIImage (solid/texture/cornerRadius/border), UIButton (5-state color/scale transition + onClick), UISlider (4 directions + drag + wholeNumbers), UIToggle (checkbox + checkmark + toggle/setOn), UIDropdown (expandable list + selectIndex), UIScrollRect (viewport + inertia + elastic bounce + scrollbars). UIInputDispatcher: pointer (down/move/up/click/enter/exit) + drag (threshold + dragStart/drag/dragEnd) + keyboard (Tab/Shift+Tab navigation) + focus management, with event bubbling + stopPropagation. UIAnimator: tween engine with 12 easing functions (linear/easeIn+Out+InOut Quad/Cubic/easeIn+Out+InOutBack/easeOutElastic/easeOutBounce), 3 loop modes (once/loop/pingPong), UISequence for sequential playback, and shortcuts (fadeIn/Out/popIn/Out/slideIn/colorTo). Pure CPU layout/hit/animation logic (no WebGL dependency), renderer consumes UIDrawCommand (rect/text/image). 69 unit tests.
uiSystem.advantage: soup3D has NO in-game UI system at all — no canvas, no widgets, no layout, no input event routing; VREEN provides a complete LyShine/UMG-class UI stack supporting HUDs, menus, dialogs, health bars, minimaps, inventory — all game UI scenarios with anchor-based responsive layout, auto-layout groups, interactive controls, pointer/keyboard/drag input, and tween animation (o3de LyShine / UE5 UMG / Unity UI Toolkit class technology)

webXR.title: WebXR VR/AR/MR (WebXR Device API / three.js / o3de Atom XR)
webXR.desc: WebXR VR/AR/MR session management system adapted from the W3C WebXR Device API, three.js WebXRManager/Controller + VRButton/ARButton, and o3de Atom XR pass. Full session lifecycle (requestSession → setSession → end) for immersive-vr / immersive-ar / inline modes with reference space management (local-floor / bounded-floor / local / viewer) and custom offset spaces for teleportation. Frame loop coordination extracts viewer pose and dispatches to the render layer (data-driven, decoupled from WebGL — core state machine testable without XR hardware). Controller registry with three spaces per controller: target ray (pointing/picking/UI), grip (handle model mount), and hand (25 joints per W3C Hand Input Module + pinch detection with hysteresis debounce). Input source sync (inputsourceschange → connect/disconnect) and button edge detection (select/squeeze start/end/click). AR subsystems: XRLightEstimation (normalized directional light + 27-coefficient spherical harmonics IBL), XRPlaneTracker (horizontal/vertical plane lifecycle + AABB bounds + nearest horizontal surface placement query), WebXRDepthSensing (depth texture + rawValueToMeters conversion + occlusion testing). WebXRProvider abstraction (BrowserWebXRProvider for production, MockWebXRProvider for tests) enables pure-logic testing without XR hardware or WebGL. DOM session buttons (createVRButton/createARButton) with feature detection + cyberpunk neon styling + sessiongranted auto-enter. 43 unit tests.
webXR.advantage: soup3D has no VR/AR/XR support at all — no WebXR, no immersive sessions, no controller tracking, no hand input, no AR light estimation/plane detection/depth sensing; VREEN provides a complete WebXR stack (VR + AR + MR) with controller + hand 25-joint tracking + pinch gestures + AR environment understanding (o3de Atom XR / three.js WebXR class technology)

filmGrain.title: Film Grain (o3de Atom FilmGrain / three.js FilmShader)
filmGrain.desc: Cinematic film grain post-processing pass adapted from o3de Atom FilmGrain.azsl + FilmGrainSettings + FilmGrainConstants. Full o3de algorithm: (1) grain UV computed via tilingScale * pixelCoord / grainTextureSize + 24fps animation offset (trunc(time * 24) mimics 24fps film frame rate, float2(0.6379, 1.7358) random skip); (2) grain sampled from precomputed noise texture (Mirror address mode) OR procedural hash21 noise (dual path); (3) luminance dampening via 4x(1-x) formula (Rec.601 luma 0.21/0.72/0.07) — grain vanishes at pure black (lum=0) and pure white (lum=1), peaks at mid-tones (lum=0.5), mimicking real film grain physical behavior; (4) replace-style lerp (rgb = lerp(rgb, grain, intensity)) per o3de, not additive. Parameters: intensity (o3de default 0.2), luminanceDampening (default 0.0), tilingScale (default 1.0), size, noiseType (hash/texture), animated (24fps). 1:1 CPU/GPU reference: filmGrainPixel() pure function + hash21() bit-exact match with GLSL, testable without WebGL. 27 unit tests.
filmGrain.advantage: soup3D has NO post-processing at all — no bloom, no tonemapping, no film grain, only a single full-screen image overlay for HUD; VREEN provides o3de Atom-class film grain with luminance dampening (4x(1-x) mid-tone peak), 24fps animation, grain texture + procedural hash dual paths, and 1:1 CPU/GPU reference for headless testing (o3de Atom FilmGrain class technology)
